status: PREREGISTERED_BY_DRIVER_UNATTESTED - Every workload parameter, generator, seed rule, statistics constant, and threshold below is frozen to the maximum ownerless extent. This plan is NOT yet the attested plan-freeze commit: host and tool identities remain OWNER_DECISION_PENDING in benchmarks/environments/, no sample may be collected, and US-008 does not pass. See benchmarks/README.md for the no-fabrication rule.
no_results_invariant: This plan contains no results and no results field may ever be added to it; the schema forbids unknown keys. Results live only in canonical raw-pair records (schemas/benchmark-raw-sample-1.0.0.schema.json) produced after the attested plan freeze and full host/tool binding.

shared_definitions.keystream: keystream(tag) is the deterministic byte stream B_0 || B_1 || ... where B_j = SHA-256(ASCII(tag + '|' + decimal(j))). lowercase-hex(s) is the lowercase hexadecimal encoding of stream s taken byte-for-byte.
shared_definitions.pacing_model: fixed-interval open-loop schedule at the stated rate; an operation issued more than 1000 ms after its schedule slot marks the sample INVALID (fail-closed, never truncated or resampled around)
shared_definitions.sample_definition: One sample run = fresh server process start, readiness probe (repeated connect + handshake at 10 ms intervals), full workload execution, metric capture, clean shutdown. One pair = one Java sample run plus one Rust sample run executed in the derived pair order. Warmup pairs (indices 0..4) execute identically and are excluded from analysis.
shared_definitions.invalid_sample_rule: An INVALID sample invalidates its entire pair. Because replacement, extension, and optional stopping are forbidden, any INVALID pair makes the whole workload run INCONCLUSIVE; the workload must be rerun in full under a new preregistered run record, never patched.

comparison_boundary.definition: Black-box TCP comparison boundary: the Java and Rust implementations are exercised only through the identical preregistered TCP endpoint below; nothing inside either process is instrumented across the boundary. Docker sbx may isolate build/test preparation but must not host measured samples (microVM overhead would change this declared boundary).

endpoint.extensions: none - permessage-deflate and every other extension disabled/not negotiated
endpoint.rationale: The PRD freezes the black-box TCP boundary but not the socket facts; a fixed loopback IPv4 endpoint with no TLS and no extensions removes negotiation degrees of freedom from both implementations equally.

peak_rss.definition: Maximum resident set size of the server process observed over the sample run.

steady_rss.definition: Resident set size of the server process after workload completion and a fixed 2-second quiesce, before shutdown.

cpu_time.definition: Total CPU time (user + system) consumed by the server process over the sample run.

startup_to_ready.definition: Elapsed time from server process exec to first successful handshake completion on the preregistered endpoint (readiness probe: repeated connect + handshake at 10 ms intervals).

latency_p50.definition: 50th percentile (nearest-rank, full unfiltered operation set) of per-operation round-trip time: last request byte written by the client to full expected response read.

allocated_bytes.definition: Cumulative bytes allocated by the server process over the sample run, read from the runtime allocator statistics interface bound at tool-identity binding.

allocation_count.definition: Cumulative allocation count, same source as allocated_bytes.

throughput.definition: Completed operations divided by elapsed time from first operation issue to last response read, per sample.

metric_endpoints.tool_identity_note: Every sampler/probe named above is a measurement tool whose exact identity and digest are OWNER_DECISION_PENDING in benchmarks/environments/; no metric may be captured before those identities bind.

workloads.title: Opening handshake and clean close
workloads.definition: Repeated WebSocket opening handshake followed immediately by a clean client-initiated close, with fixed cycle count and pacing.

rate.rationale: 20-second nominal sample at 1000 cycles; low enough that loopback accept queues never saturate, so the metric isolates handshake cost, not backlog behavior.
rate.pacing: fixed-interval open-loop schedule at the stated rate; an operation issued more than 1000 ms after its schedule slot marks the sample INVALID (fail-closed, never truncated or resampled around)

concurrency.rationale: A single serial connection isolates per-handshake cost; concurrency pressure is covered by wl-06.

operations.rationale: Large enough to dominate scheduling noise on a 20-second sample, small enough for a bounded run.

hard_timeout_seconds.rationale: Fail-closed cap: a sample exceeding it is INVALID, never truncated.

inputs.definition: Each cycle i (0..999): TCP connect to the preregistered endpoint; HTTP/1.1 GET / handshake with Host: 127.0.0.1:9101, Upgrade: websocket, Connection: Upgrade, Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13, Sec-WebSocket-Key = base64(first 16 bytes of SHA-256(ASCII('vjwp-us008|wl-01|key|' + decimal(i)))); no extensions, no subprotocol. After the 101 response, the client sends a masked close frame, status code 1000, empty reason.
inputs.rationale: The PRD freezes the workload class; the exact deterministic key generator and cycle shape are the driver's preregistered choice.

outputs.definition: Per cycle: an HTTP 101 response carrying the correct RFC 6455 Sec-WebSocket-Accept for the sent key; a close frame with status code 1000 from the server; orderly TCP shutdown. Any deviation marks the sample INVALID.
outputs.rationale: Exact expected bytes/close codes fixed so success is machine-checkable with no post-hoc discretion.

workloads.title: Small text echo
workloads.definition: Small text frames echoed over one established connection with fixed message size, count, and pacing.

rate.rationale: 20-second nominal sample at 10000 echoes; well below loopback saturation so per-message cost, not queuing, is measured.
rate.pacing: fixed-interval open-loop schedule at the stated rate; an operation issued more than 1000 ms after its schedule slot marks the sample INVALID (fail-closed, never truncated or resampled around)

concurrency.rationale: Single-connection serial echo isolates per-message framing cost.

operations.rationale: 10000 echoes give stable per-operation latency percentiles.

hard_timeout_seconds.rationale: Fail-closed cap: a sample exceeding it is INVALID, never truncated.

inputs.definition: One connection per sample (handshake as wl-01 with key tag 'vjwp-us008|wl-02|key|'). Echo i (0..9999): a single masked text frame (FIN=1, opcode 0x1) whose 128-byte payload is the first 128 bytes of lowercase-hex(keystream('vjwp-us008|wl-02|payload|' + decimal(i))); hex encoding keeps every payload valid UTF-8. After echo 9999 the client sends close 1000.
inputs.rationale: The PRD freezes the workload class; the 128-byte size and deterministic generator are the driver's preregistered choice of 'small'.

outputs.definition: Each echo returns exactly one text message whose payload bytes equal the sent payload; final close 1000. Any mismatch marks the sample INVALID.
outputs.rationale: Byte-identical echo expectation removes output discretion.

workloads.title: Fragmented 64 KiB binary echo
workloads.definition: 64 KiB binary messages sent as a fixed fragmentation pattern and echoed, with fixed message count and pacing.

rate.rationale: 20-second nominal sample at 1000 messages; the offered load (50 x 65536 bytes ~= 3.1 MiB/s) is well below loopback bandwidth so reassembly cost, not transport, dominates.
rate.pacing: fixed-interval open-loop schedule at the stated rate; an operation issued more than 1000 ms after its schedule slot marks the sample INVALID (fail-closed, never truncated or resampled around)

operations.rationale: 1000 messages bound the run while exercising 16000 fragment events.

hard_timeout_seconds.rationale: Fail-closed cap sized for the larger payload volume: a sample exceeding it is INVALID.

inputs.definition: One connection per sample (handshake as wl-01 with key tag 'vjwp-us008|wl-03|key|'). Message i (0..999): 65536 bytes = first 65536 bytes of keystream('vjwp-us008|wl-03|payload|' + decimal(i)), sent as exactly 16 masked fragments of 4096 bytes each: first frame FIN=0 opcode 0x2, then 15 continuation frames (opcode 0x0), the last with FIN=1. After message 999 the client sends close 1000.
inputs.rationale: The 64 KiB (65536-byte) message size is PRD_VERBATIM; the 16 x 4096-byte fragmentation schedule, rate, and count are the driver's preregistered choice.

outputs.definition: Each message is echoed as one binary message whose reassembled payload equals the 65536 sent bytes; the server's own fragmentation of its echo is unconstrained. Final close 1000. Any payload mismatch marks the sample INVALID.
outputs.rationale: Reassembled-payload equality is the black-box observable; server-side fragmentation is not part of the boundary.

workloads.title: Ping/pong/close control-frame mix
workloads.definition: A fixed deterministic interleaving of text data frames with ping, pong, and close control frames.

rate.unit: operations per second (50 nine-operation cycles per second)
rate.rationale: 20-second nominal sample at 9000 operations, matching wl-02's per-operation pacing regime.
rate.pacing: fixed-interval open-loop schedule at the stated rate; an operation issued more than 1000 ms after its schedule slot marks the sample INVALID (fail-closed, never truncated or resampled around)

concurrency.rationale: Single connection isolates control-frame handling cost.

operations.unit: operations (1000 cycles of the frozen 9-operation sequence)
operations.rationale: 1000 cycles exercise 2000 pings, 1000 unsolicited pongs, and 6000 echoes deterministically.

hard_timeout_seconds.rationale: Fail-closed cap: a sample exceeding it is INVALID, never truncated.

inputs.definition: One connection per sample (handshake as wl-01 with key tag 'vjwp-us008|wl-04|key|'). Cycle c (0..999) is the frozen 9-operation sequence: operations 1-6 are 128-byte text echoes with payload = first 128 bytes of lowercase-hex(keystream('vjwp-us008|wl-04|text|' + decimal(6*c+k))) for k=0..5; operation 7 is a masked ping whose 125-byte payload is the first 125 bytes of keystream('vjwp-us008|wl-04|ping|' + decimal(c)); operation 8 is a masked ping with empty payload; operation 9 is an unsolicited masked pong whose 4-byte payload is the first 4 bytes of keystream('vjwp-us008|wl-04|pong|' + decimal(c)). After cycle 999 the client sends close 1000.
inputs.rationale: The PRD freezes the control-mix class; the exact 9-operation schedule and generators are the driver's preregistered choice (125 bytes is the RFC 6455 control-payload maximum).

outputs.definition: Per cycle: six byte-identical text echoes; a pong echoing the 125-byte ping payload; a pong with empty payload for the empty ping; no response to the unsolicited pong. Final close frame with status code 1000. Any deviation marks the sample INVALID.
outputs.rationale: RFC 6455 fixes pong semantics; freezing them as expected outputs removes discretion.

workloads.title: Cap-before-allocation rejection
workloads.definition: Frames declaring a payload larger than the configured cap must be rejected before payload allocation, with fixed oversize inputs.

rate.rationale: 20-second nominal sample at 500 rejection cycles; each cycle is a full connect-reject-close round trip.
rate.pacing: fixed-interval open-loop schedule at the stated rate; an operation issued more than 1000 ms after its schedule slot marks the sample INVALID (fail-closed, never truncated or resampled around)

operations.rationale: 500 cycles bound the run while giving stable rejection-path statistics.

hard_timeout_seconds.rationale: Fail-closed cap: a sample exceeding it is INVALID, never truncated.

server_configuration.definition: Both implementations are configured with a maximum incoming message/frame payload cap of exactly 1048576 bytes (1 MiB), and no other limit overrides.
server_configuration.rationale: A concrete identical cap is required for a byte-identical rejection boundary; 1 MiB is the driver's preregistered choice.

inputs.definition: Connection i (0..499): handshake as wl-01 with key tag 'vjwp-us008|wl-05|key|', then one masked binary frame (FIN=1, opcode 0x2) with declared payload length 2097152 bytes (2 MiB, double the cap), payload bytes streamed from keystream('vjwp-us008|wl-05|payload|' + decimal(i)).
inputs.rationale: Double-the-cap declared length forces the cap check to fire on the frame header, before allocation.

outputs.definition: The server must reject on the declared length before allocating or consuming the oversized payload: a close frame with status code 1009 (message too big) followed by TCP close. Echoing the message, or reading the full 2 MiB before closing, marks the sample INVALID.
outputs.rationale: RFC 6455 section 7.4.1 defines 1009 for messages too big to process; cap-before-allocation is the preregistered semantic under test.

workloads.title: Bounded concurrent connection/command pressure
workloads.definition: Bounded concurrent connection churn plus echo traffic at fixed per-worker rates and fixed concurrency.

rate.unit: echo operations per second per worker (1600 aggregate at full concurrency)
rate.rationale: Per-worker pacing keeps aggregate load bounded and deterministic.
rate.pacing: fixed-interval open-loop schedule at the stated rate; an operation issued more than 1000 ms after its schedule slot marks the sample INVALID (fail-closed, never truncated or resampled around)

concurrency.rationale: 64 workers exercise concurrent accept, read, and write paths while staying far from loopback fd limits.

operations.unit: operations total: 64 workers x 5 connection cycles x (1 handshake + 50 echoes) = 320 connection cycles + 16000 echoes
operations.rationale: Fixed worker/cycle/echo counts bound the run deterministically.

nominal_duration_seconds.rationale: Five 2-second echo phases per worker plus connection churn overhead.

hard_timeout_seconds.rationale: Fail-closed cap sized for 64-way concurrency: a sample exceeding it is INVALID.

inputs.definition: 64 concurrent workers start together at sample begin. Worker w (0..63) performs 5 sequential connection cycles; in cycle c (0..4): handshake as wl-01 with key tag 'vjwp-us008|wl-06|key|' + decimal(w) + '|' + decimal(c), then 50 echoes k (0..49) each a single masked binary frame (FIN=1, opcode 0x2) whose 512-byte payload is the first 512 bytes of keystream('vjwp-us008|wl-06|payload|' + decimal(w) + '|' + decimal(c) + '|' + decimal(k)), then client close 1000.
inputs.rationale: The PRD freezes the bounded-pressure class; worker count, churn schedule, payload size, and generators are the driver's preregistered choice.

outputs.definition: All 16000 echoes return byte-identical binary payloads; all 320 connection cycles complete with server close handling for code 1000; zero refused or failed connections. Any failure marks the sample INVALID.
outputs.rationale: Zero-failure expectation makes saturation observable as sample invalidity instead of silent degradation.

pairing_and_ordering.seed_derivation_rule: seed_string(workload) = 'vjwp-us008-pair-order|v1|' + workload_id. For pair index i in 0..34: digest = SHA-256(ASCII(seed_string + '|' + decimal(i))); order[i] = JAVA_FIRST if digest[0] is even, RUST_FIRST if odd. Pairs 0..4 are warmup (excluded), pairs 5..34 are measured. Executable reference implementation: internal/benchplan.PairOrder; every derived_pair_order above is machine-verified against this rule by 'benchplanctl verify' and the package tests, and was independently derived with a second (Python hashlib) implementation before being frozen here.
pairing_and_ordering.provenance: 5 warmup + 30 measured pairs and deterministic SHA-256-seeded randomized Java/Rust order are PRD_VERBATIM; the exact seed string format and first-byte-parity rule are PREREGISTERED_BY_DRIVER (rationale: a pure hash of frozen public strings admits no discretion and cannot be re-rolled after results are known).

statistics.per_endpoint_analysis: For every preregistered endpoint (workload x metric): all 30 paired natural-log Rust/Java ratios ln(rust/java); their arithmetic mean; the sample standard deviation (n-1 denominator); the two-sided 95% Student-t interval with 29 degrees of freedom (critical value t_0.975,29 = 2.045230 per published tables); and the exponentiated interval bounds. Reference implementation: internal/benchplan.AnalyzePairs, validated against published t-tables, an independent Simpson-rule integration of the t density, and closed-form synthetic fixtures labeled SYNTHETIC_FIXTURE_NOT_A_MEASUREMENT.

power_model.underpowered_rule: An observed sample log-ratio SD above max_log_ratio_sd makes the endpoint INCONCLUSIVE (underpowered relative to the frozen model); it is never rescued by resampling, extension, or outlier deletion.

memory.rationale: The memory alternative: Rust peak/steady RSS at most 80% of Java's, matching the 0.8 upper-CI threshold on the RSS endpoints. The PRD names the alternative class; the size is the driver's preregistered choice.

non_regression.rationale: The non-regression alternative: a 10% regression on any non-memory endpoint must be detectable. At sd=0.10, n=30, alpha=0.025, power 0.8 the minimum detectable |log effect| is approximately 0.053 < ln(1.1) = 0.0953; machine-verified by internal/benchplan.VerifyPowerModel via 'benchplanctl verify'.

statistics.decision_rule: Only complete predeclared paired evidence can decide. Altered summaries, omissions, identity mismatches, nonfinite values, or raw-versus-summary disagreement are INCONCLUSIVE and blocking. Reference implementation: internal/benchplan.DecideEndpoint (fail-closed; validated on synthetic fixtures for the valid, underpowered, noisy, reordered, missing, extra, and post-hoc-mutated cases).

ci_thresholds.note: Ratios are Rust/Java; bounds are exponentiated 95% CI bounds. 'upper' means the exponentiated upper bound must be <= value; 'lower' means the exponentiated lower bound must be >= value. Applied per workload, per metric endpoint.

run_validity.thermal_power_identity: fail-closed: any thermal throttle event, power-state anomaly, or host/tool identity mismatch during a run invalidates the run (INCONCLUSIVE, never patched or resampled around)

binding.note: Canonical raw pairs must bind the plan, workload, order, environments, tools, future Java/Rust source/executable/adapter digests, and the independently rebuilt analyzer. None of these digests exists yet; none is fabricated. internal/benchplan.DecideEndpoint refuses any MEASURED sample set whose bindings are missing, malformed, or zero.
environment_bindings: benchmarks/environments/confirmation.json (binding_status UNBOUND: every host field OWNER_DECISION_PENDING)
binding.analyzer_digest: NOT_MEASURED (the independently rebuilt analyzer identity binds with the tool identities)
